episodes.188822: A passing upper-level trough spawned a band of strong storms which produced wind gusts near 40 mph as activity moved offshore of the local Atlantic coast in the evening.
episodes.189304: A couple waves of strong to severe storms moved across the region ahead of a cold front under passing short wave troughs.
episodes.190058: A strong low over the eastern Pacific Ocean sent an associated trough to the southern Oregon coast. Waterspouts developed as this trough neared the coast.
episodes.190186: Isolated strong thunderstorms developed ahead of a passing cold front in the late evening hours across portions of southeast Georgia. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce a few instances of hail.
episodes.190187: A cold front tracked eastwards across North Carolina while at the same time low pressure tracked northeastwards along this cold front the morning of March twenty-eighth. As this occurred a line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across the Coastal Plain and quickly tracked eastwards as well impacted the waters from Onslow Bay northeastwards into portions of the Neuse and Bay Rivers as well as the Croatan Sound with thunderstorms bringing damaging winds to these waters. Thunderstorm activity quickly pushed away from the area by mid morning.
episodes.190470: Scattered gale-force wind gusts associated with thunderstorms occurred as a pre-frontal trough pushed southeast through the Florida Keys.
